step: Second mechanism search — outside 4 exhausted causal families

ceo_directive_compliance.directive: Search for mechanisms that change the rescue problem itself, rather than changing the actuator. Candidate space should include: in-situ obstruction prevention, self-clearing geometry, reversible lumen rerouting, sacrificial flow paths, external noncontact mechanical excitation, or other mechanisms that restore function without pulling or pushing debris toward the brain. Every new candidate starts at zero.
ceo_directive_compliance.pushing_the_envelope: Never strengthen a negative result beyond its evidence. A false negative can destroy the best invention we could have found.

constraint_1_traction_against_ingrowth.statement: Any mechanism that relies on traction (pulling) against a permanently implanted endovascular anchor faces tissue ingrowth resistance. The eShunt anchor is DESIGNED for ingrowth. After 6+ months, retrieval success drops to ~50% (IVC filter data).
constraint_1_traction_against_ingrowth.what_it_eliminates: All PULLING mechanisms (snare, traction, catheter extraction)
constraint_1_traction_against_ingrowth.what_it_does_NOT_eliminate: Mechanisms that don't pull (push, dissolve, reroute, prevent)

constraint_2_fragmentation_embolization.statement: Zero embolization is a justified safety gate (FDA precedent, pulmonary embolism risk). Any mechanism that produces fragments (degradation, mechanical breaking, tissue tearing) in the venous system is unsafe.
constraint_2_fragmentation_embolization.what_it_eliminates: All FRAGMENTING mechanisms (bioresorbable, mechanical tearing, cutting)
constraint_2_fragmentation_embolization.what_it_does_NOT_eliminate: Mechanisms that don't fragment (flow-based, geometric, preventive)

constraint_3_proximal_debris_transport.statement: Retrograde flow pushes debris toward the brain (SAS). The eShunt's venous drainage direction means retrograde = brain-ward. Clinical hazard is analogical (SAH, arachnoiditis), not directly proven.
constraint_3_proximal_debris_transport.what_it_eliminates: All RETROGRADE FLUSH mechanisms that mobilize debris proximally
constraint_3_proximal_debris_transport.what_it_does_NOT_eliminate: Mechanisms that push debris DISTALLY (toward venous system) or don't mobilize debris at all

constraint_4_magnetic_actuation_limitati.statement: Magnetic actuation is incompatible with MRI (gatekeeper for neurosurgical implants). Force at 5-10cm depth (1/r³) is 10-50x insufficient.
constraint_4_magnetic_actuation_limitati.what_it_eliminates: All MAGNETIC mechanisms (MRI incompatibility, force insufficiency)

constraint_5_mri_compatibility.statement: Any eShunt modification must be MRI-compatible. Hydrocephalus patients need brain MRI for follow-up.
constraint_5_mri_compatibility.what_it_eliminates: Ferromagnetic materials, RF-heating elements, MRI-artifact-creating components
constraint_5_mri_compatibility.what_it_does_NOT_eliminate: MRI-safe materials, non-conductive components, small artifacts outside imaging region

constraint_synthesis.what_is_eliminated: Pulling (ingrowth), fragmenting (embolization), retrograde flushing (debris to brain), magnetic actuation (MRI + force)
constraint_synthesis.what_remains_possible: Mechanisms that: (a) PREVENT obstruction rather than clear it, (b) push debris DISTALLY (toward venous system, not brain), (c) reroute flow without mobilizing debris, (d) use non-magnetic external actuation, (e) change the eShunt geometry to be self-clearing
constraint_synthesis.key_shift: The first 4 candidates all tried to SOLVE an existing obstruction (retrieve, dissolve, flush, magnetically release). The second search should focus on PREVENTING obstruction or RESTORING flow without debris mobilization.

new_candidate_search.approach: The CEO's suggested directions: in-situ obstruction prevention, self-clearing geometry, reversible lumen rerouting, sacrificial flow paths, external noncontact mechanical excitation.

candidates.name: Self-clearing geometry — hydrodynamic design that prevents obstruction accumulation
candidates.mechanism: Redesign the eShunt lumen geometry so that normal CSF flow naturally prevents protein/cellular accumulation. Examples: expanding lumen cross-section at potential stagnation points, helical flow inducers that create secondary flow preventing deposition, or surface texturing that discourages adhesion.
candidates.how_it_changes_the_problem: PREVENTS obstruction rather than treating it. No retrieval, no flush, no debris mobilization. The eShunt doesn't get obstructed in the first place.

constraint_check.mri: PASS — geometric modification, no MRI-unsafe materials

candidates.prior_art_concern: Surface texturing and flow optimization for shunt catheters may be known. Need claim-level search.

candidates.name: Reversible lumen rerouting — bypass obstruction through secondary channel
candidates.mechanism: The eShunt has a primary lumen (normal flow path) and a secondary bypass lumen (normally closed). When the primary lumen obstructs, the secondary lumen opens (mechanically or pressure-activated), restoring CSF drainage without clearing the obstruction. The obstruction remains in place but is bypassed.
candidates.how_it_changes_the_problem: RESTORES flow without mobilizing debris. The obstruction stays where it is; flow reroutes around it. No retrieval, no flush, no debris to brain.
candidates.prior_art_concern: Bypass lumens exist in vascular stents (dual-lumen). Need to check if applied to CSF shunts specifically.

candidates.name: Pressure-activated self-clearing — obstruction triggers autonomous pressure release
candidates.mechanism: The eShunt has a pressure-activated valve that opens when obstruction raises the pressure gradient above a threshold (e.g., >12 mmHg). When the obstruction builds up and pressure rises, the valve opens wider, increasing flow velocity through the obstruction, potentially flushing it distally (toward the venous system, NOT toward the brain). The debris goes WHERE IT'S SUPPOSED TO GO — into the venous drainage.
candidates.how_it_changes_the_problem: Uses the OBSTRUCTION ITSELF as the trigger. Debris is pushed DISTALLY (toward venous system, same direction as normal flow). No retrograde, no brain-ward debris. The eShunt self-regulates.

constraint_check.fragmentation: LOW RISK — debris is pushed intact, not fragmented
constraint_check.retrograde_debris: PASS — debris goes DISTALLY (toward venous system), same as normal flow direction

candidates.prior_art_concern: Pressure-activated valves exist in shunts. The novel aspect would be using pressure to FLUSH obstruction distally rather than just regulate drainage.
candidates.key_advantage: This is the first candidate that pushes debris in the SAFE direction (distal/venous) rather than the dangerous direction (proximal/brain). All 4 V8 candidates either didn't address debris direction (R1, R2, R4) or pushed it the WRONG way (R3).

candidates.name: External noncontact ultrasound excitation — break obstruction via acoustic force
candidates.mechanism: External ultrasound transducer applies focused acoustic energy to the eShunt obstruction site. Acoustic radiation force breaks the obstruction into small particles that are carried DISTALLY by normal CSF flow (toward venous system). No catheter, no magnetic component, no implant modification.
candidates.how_it_changes_the_problem: Uses EXTERNAL energy (ultrasound) to break obstruction without any implanted actuator. Debris goes distally (normal flow direction). No retrieval, no retrograde, no MRI concern.

constraint_check.fragmentation: CONCERN — ultrasound breaks obstruction into particles. But particles are carried DISTALLY (toward venous system), not proximally (toward brain). Venous system can tolerate small particles better than SAS.
constraint_check.retrograde_debris: PASS — debris goes distally, same as normal flow

candidates.prior_art_concern: Ultrasound is used for kidney stone fragmentation (lithotripsy) and clot disruption (sonothrombolysis). Need to check if applied to CSF shunt obstruction.

candidates.name: Sacrificial flow path — designed obstruction zone with replaceable cartridge
candidates.mechanism: The eShunt has a designed 'sacrificial zone' where obstruction is EXPECTED to occur (narrowest point, highest fouling). This zone is a replaceable cartridge that can be exchanged endovascularly without removing the entire eShunt. When obstruction occurs, the cartridge is exchanged (like changing a filter), not the entire device.
candidates.how_it_changes_the_problem: Changes from 'retrieve the whole eShunt' to 'exchange a small cartridge.' The ingrowth problem is avoided because the anchoring part (permanent) is separate from the obstructing part (replaceable).

constraint_check.ingrowth: PARTIAL — the anchoring part is permanent (ingrown), but the cartridge is SEPARATE and replaceable without dislodging the anchor
constraint_check.fragmentation: LOW RISK — cartridge exchange is mechanical but doesn't require tearing through tissue
constraint_check.retrograde_debris: DEPENDS — cartridge exchange may mobilize some debris, but it can be designed to push distally

candidates.prior_art_concern: Replaceable filters/cartridges exist in industrial applications. Need to check if applied to CSF shunts or endovascular devices.

constraint_filtering_results.R5_self_clearing_geometry: ADVANCES — no constraint conflicts. Prevents rather than treats.
constraint_filtering_results.R6_reversible_lumen_rerouting: ADVANCES — no constraint conflicts. Bypasses without mobilizing.
constraint_filtering_results.R7_pressure_activated_distal_flush: ADVANCES — KEY CANDIDATE. First to push debris in SAFE direction (distal/venous). Addresses the fundamental R3 problem (debris direction) by reversing it — debris goes where it SHOULD go.
constraint_filtering_results.R8_ultrasound_excitation: ADVANCES — external, non-magnetic, distal debris. But fragmentation risk remains (CE-007 concern for venous-side particles).
constraint_filtering_results.R9_sacrificial_cartridge: ADVANCES — separates anchoring (permanent) from obstruction (replaceable). Novel approach to ingrowth problem.

ranking.rationale: First candidate to push debris in SAFE direction. Uses obstruction itself as trigger. No external actuation. Self-regulating. Addresses the fundamental problem that killed R3 (debris direction).
PREVENTS rather than treats. No debris, no retrieval, no actuation. But may not work for all obstruction types (protein vs cellular vs thrombotic).
Bypasses obstruction without mobilizing. But adds complexity (second lumen) and may eventually obstruct too.
Novel approach to ingrowth. But cartridge exchange still requires endovascular procedure and may mobilize debris.
External, non-magnetic. But fragmentation risk and unknown if ultrasound can reach eShunt depth effectively.

next_step: Attack R7 (pressure-activated distal flush) from zero through full Article XX + physics + prior art pipeline. R7 is the leading candidate because it changes the debris DIRECTION (distal instead of proximal), which is the fundamental difference from all 4 failed V8 candidates.
